name: Rowan Halebrook
about: Rowan is a fictional vestibular physiotherapist who talks with people about dizziness, balance, and motion sensitivity after a concussion. A visit is a chance to describe those symptoms and ask what kind of follow-up to raise with a GP. This profile is sample data for the demo.

name: Mira Quillan
about: Mira is a fictional vestibular physiotherapist focused on balance and inner-ear symptoms that can linger after a concussion. People use this kind of visit to walk through what sets their dizziness off and what to mention at their next GP appointment. This listing is not a real clinic.

name: Ellis Northvale
about: Ellis is a fictional vision therapist who meets people bothered by reading strain, double vision, or light sensitivity after a concussion. The conversation is about those visual symptoms and which questions to bring back to a doctor. This profile is placeholder data only.

name: Sable Fenwick
about: Sable is a fictional vision therapist who helps people describe screen fatigue, focusing trouble, and visual discomfort after a concussion. A visit is for sorting those details before a conversation with a GP. This clinic name is invented for the demo.

name: Jonah Bramble
about: Jonah is a fictional sleep specialist who talks with people about trouble falling asleep, waking often, or daytime sleepiness after a concussion. The visit is a place to map those sleep patterns and decide what to raise with a GP. This profile is sample data.

name: Priya Mossglen
about: Priya is a fictional sleep specialist who meets people whose nights have stayed unsettled after a concussion. Together they review sleep habits and the questions worth taking to a doctor. This listing does not represent a real practitioner.

name: Casey Whitlow
about: Casey is a fictional psychologist who talks with people about mood, worry, and the mental load that can follow a concussion. A visit is for naming those experiences and choosing what to discuss with a GP. This profile is fictional demo data.

name: Harper Voss
about: Harper is a fictional psychologist who meets people dealing with irritability, low mood, or feeling overwhelmed after a concussion. The conversation stays on what they are noticing and which questions to bring to a doctor. This clinic is invented for the demo.

name: Theo Marlowe
about: Theo is a fictional physiotherapist who talks with people about neck pain, stiffness, and everyday movement after a concussion. A visit is a chance to describe those body symptoms and what to mention at a GP appointment. This profile is placeholder data.

name: Lila Pembroke
about: Lila is a fictional sports medicine physician who meets people sorting return-to-activity questions after a concussion. The visit is for gathering those questions to take to a GP, not for a diagnosis or a promised outcome. This listing is sample data only.

name: Nia Calder
about: Nia is a fictional sports medicine physician who talks with people about how activity and energy line up after a concussion. A visit is for writing those details down to take to a GP or pediatric clinician. This profile is sample data, not a treatment plan.

name: Owen Hartwell
about: Owen is a fictional sports medicine physician who meets adults sorting activity and energy questions after a concussion. The visit gathers those questions for a GP. This listing is invented for the demo and is marked for adults.

name: June Pell
about: June is a fictional physiotherapist who talks with people about neck comfort and sensitivity to light or sound after a concussion. A visit is for describing those symptoms to take to a GP or pediatric clinician. This clinic is not real.

name: Willa Thornberry
about: Willa is a fictional family physician. People use a visit to gather questions after a concussion and decide what to raise next. This clinic is invented for the demo and is not a real practice.

name: Ned Plumwick
about: Ned is a fictional family physician. A visit is for listing what someone has noticed after a concussion so those notes can be reviewed. This listing does not represent a real person or clinic.

name: Nell Amberly
about: Nell is a fictional optometrist who talks with people about eye strain, focusing, and tracking after a concussion. A visit is a chance to describe those visual symptoms and decide what to raise with a GP. This profile is sample data for the demo.

name: Felix Dunmore
about: Felix is a fictional optometrist who meets people bothered by reading fatigue or screen strain after a concussion. The conversation is about those symptoms and which questions to take to a doctor. This clinic is invented for the demo.
